structure: Part 7, "Declaration, confirmation, delete and cancel amendment": the four feature folders that end a live-animals notification, read in full from repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend on main — src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/{declaration,confirmation,delete-notification,cancel-amend}. Each folder holds page.js (id, slug, maturity), controller.js (Hapi routes and handlers), template.njk (Nunjucks, extending shared/layout.njk), copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js, and a co-located Playwright fit spec; declaration also has test-support.js and confirmation also has outstanding.js. Four pages are covered. (1) Declaration, /notifications/{journeyId}/declaration (GET and POST, slug 'declaration', maturity 'detailing'): a statements-and-one-checkbox page rendered only by POSTing step=review from the review page — its GET always redirects — with one required confirmation checkbox, a date-of-declaration line, a Continue button, and seven refusal paths (already-submitted, opened-before-review, unknown-step, changed-since-review, review-not-recorded, review-refused, not-ready-to-submit) that all redirect to the confirmation or the review. (2) Confirmation, /notifications/{journeyId}/confirmation (GET only, maturity 'detailing'): a govukPanel carrying the reference number, a conditional outstanding-items section computed by outstanding.js, then three fixed sections — Transporting the consignment, How to view or amend this notification (dashboard link plus a POST button that starts a new notification), and Getting help (APHA email, telephone, APHA Service Desk email, opening hours, HMRC and call-charges links) — and no back link. (3) Delete, /notifications/{journeyId}/delete (GET and POST, slug 'delete', maturity 'detailing'): a question-as-H1 confirmation page with a warning Yes button and a secondary No button back to the dashboard, allowed only for a draft, submitted or amending notification, redirecting to the dashboard with ?deleted=1 on success. (4) Cancel amendment, /notifications/{journeyId}/cancel-amend (GET and POST, slug from the shared kit, maturity 'detailing'): the same two-button shape, allowed only while the notification is amending, restoring the submitted snapshot and returning to the notification view with ?cancelled=1. The part also covers every behaviour the four fit specs prove (declaration 398 lines, confirmation 190, delete-notification 105, cancel-amend 192), including the axe checks and the no-JavaScript cancel-amendment path, and key parity between each copy.cy.js and its English twin. Routes are read against src/server/app/shared/paths.js (pageRoutePath = /notifications/{journeyId}/<slug>) and the slug constants in src/server/app/shared/kit.js (CYA_SLUG = 'notification-view', CANCEL_AMEND_SLUG = 'cancel-amend'); the engine helpers softDeleteJourney and cancelAmendJourney in src/server/app/engine/journey.js are cited only where a controller's observable outcome depends on them. The part stops at the review page (part 6) and the notification list (part 4): copy owned by shared/, check-answers or dashboard is cited but not claimed.

claims.statement: Opening the declaration URL directly never shows the declaration page: a GET on a submitted notification redirects to its confirmation page.
A GET on the declaration URL for any notification that is not submitted redirects to the review page.
A typed or bookmarked declaration URL sends the user to the review page instead.
The declaration page is shown only by posting step=review, which is what the review page's submit button does.

claims.statement: A posted concurrency token that is absent or empty is treated as no token at all, so such a submit is refused as changed-since-review.
claims.quote:
const postedConcurrencyToken = (payload) =>
  payload.concurrencyToken == null || payload.concurrencyToken === ''
    ? undefined
    : Number(payload.concurrencyToken)
claims.note: mechanism: parses the posted token; it follows that undefined can never equal a real journey.concurrencyToken, so line 190's check refuses.

claims.statement: The cancel-amendment confirmation page lives at /notifications/{journeyId}/cancel-amend and answers both GET and POST.
claims.note: the slug comes from the shared kit (CANCEL_AMEND_SLUG = 'cancel-amend', src/server/app/shared/kit.js:71) rather than from the page's own page.js, which declares only an id and a maturity.

claims.statement: The cancel-amendment page's H1 is "Cancel this amendment?"
claims.quote: title: 'Cancel this amendment?',
claims.note: the same string is the page title and the H1.

claims.statement: The cancel-amendment page explains "Your changes since you started amending will be discarded and the submitted version restored."
claims.quote: body: 'Your changes since you started amending will be discarded and the submitted version restored.',

claims.statement: The cancel-amendment page offers a standard (not warning) button "Yes, cancel amendment" that submits the form.
claims.quote: {{ govukButton({ text: copy.confirmButton }) }}
claims.note: this differs from the delete page, whose confirm button carries govuk-button--warning.

claims.statement: The cancel-amendment page offers a secondary button "No, return to notification" that links back to the notification view.
claims.note: noHref is the notification view path for this notification.

claims.statement: Choosing "No, return to notification" keeps the amendment and the value changed during it, and returns to the notification view headed as a resubmission.
claims.quote:
await expect(
      page.getByRole('heading', { name: checkAnswersCopy.resubmittingTitle })
    ).toBeVisible()
    await expectAmendStrip(page)
    await expect(page.getByText('DiscardMe99', { exact: true })).toBeVisible()

claims.statement: The cancel-amendment page's back link returns to the notification view.
The cancel-amendment page can only be opened while the notification is being amended.
Opening the cancel-amendment page for a submitted notification sends the user to that notification's view page, and for any other state to the dashboard.
claims.quote:
const nonAmendTarget = (journey) =>
  journey.status === state.SUBMITTED
    ? cyaPath(journey.journeyId)
    : dashboardPath()

claims.statement: A cancel-amendment posted for a notification that is not being amended is ignored and redirected the same way as the GET.
A refused cancel amendment is logged as "Cancel amend refused" with the notification id, its status and the reason not-in-amend.
Confirming the cancel restores the submitted version of the notification and returns to its view page with the query cancelled=1, which shows the cancel-amendment success banner.
claims.quote:
return restored
    ? h.redirect(`${cyaPath(restored.journeyId)}?cancelled=1`)
    : h.redirect(dashboardPath())
claims.note: the banner wording is checkAnswersCopy.cancelAmend.successBody, owned by the check-answers feature (part 6).

claims.statement: After the cancel, the restored notification view is tagged Submitted, the value changed during the amendment is gone, the previously submitted value is back and no Change links are offered.
claims.quote:
await expect(page.getByText('DiscardMe99', { exact: true })).toHaveCount(0)
    await expect(
      page.getByText(values.internalReferenceNumber, { exact: true })
    ).toBeVisible()
    await expect(page.getByRole('link', { name: /^Change/ })).toHaveCount(0)

claims.statement: Back from the restored submitted notification view opens the notification list.
claims.quote:
await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Back', exact: true }).click()

    await expect(page).toHaveURL(BASE)

claims.statement: Cancelling an amendment on a notification this browser session does not know about restores nothing and returns to the dashboard.
claims.note: mechanism: the engine returns undefined for an unknown notification, so the controller takes its dashboard redirect. Recorded as an access-control behaviour of the cancel action; no exploit detail is given.

claims.statement: When the cancel fails recoverably, the cancel-amendment page is redisplayed with a recoverable-error state and HTTP 500.
claims.quote:
() =>
      render(h, journey, { recoverableError: true }).code(
        HTTP_STATUS_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
      )

claims.statement: A "Cancel amend" link is offered in the amendment status strip on the notification's question pages and its view page while an amendment is in progress.
The cancel-amendment page itself still shows the Amend status strip but does not offer the Cancel amend link again.
claims.quote: offerCancelAmend: false

claims.statement: The cancel-amendment URL may carry a from query naming the page the user came from.
claims.quote: await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/cancel-amend(?:\?from=[^#]*)?$/)
claims.note: the query is tolerated by the spec rather than required; the link that sets it is built in the shared kit, not in this feature.

claims.statement: Cancelling an amendment works with JavaScript turned off: the status bar's Cancel amend link reaches the confirmation page and Yes restores the Submitted notification.
The cancel-amendment form posts the CSRF crumb and the notification's concurrency token, but the cancel is carried out without comparing that token, so a cancel is never refused as stale.
claims.quote:
<input type="hidden" name="crumb" value="{{ crumb }}" />
    <input type="hidden" name="concurrencyToken" value="{{ concurrencyToken }}" />
claims.note: mechanism: the token comes from kit.base (journey.concurrencyToken) and is posted, but the handler passes only the journey id to cancelAmendJourney, which does not read request.payload.

claims.statement: The cancel-amendment page is at maturity level "detailing", so its behaviour is not signed off.
claims.quote: export const cancelAmendPage = { id: 'cancel-amend', maturity: 'detailing' }

claims.statement: The cancel-amendment page and the restored submitted notification view both have no serious or critical accessibility violations.
claims.quote: await expectNoSeriousOrCriticalViolations(page, 'Cancel amendment')
claims.note: the second check is labelled 'Read-only submitted check answers'.

claims.statement: The cancel-amendment page asks its question with two buttons rather than a radio question, so it has no option list and no validation message: pressing Yes acts straight away.
claims.note: the part's scope expects "the question and its options" and "the validation message". The template holds no radios, the copy file holds no errors key, and the controller runs no validate() call. Looked in template.njk, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js and controller.js, and there is no validate.js in the folder.

claims.statement: The Welsh cancel-amendment copy carries exactly the same four keys as the English file, with no key missing or extra, and is marked as an unreviewed machine draft.
claims.quote: // MACHINE-DRAFT Welsh — not reviewed by a translator. Do not ship user-facing without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
claims.note: keys compared: title, body, confirmButton, noLink.

claims.statement: Pressing Continue on an incomplete amendment is refused: the notification view is reloaded with the query refused=1, shows the "There is a problem" error summary naming the unfinished card, and keeps the Amend status strip.
claims.quote:
await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/notification-view\?refused=1$/)
    await expect(
      page.getByRole('heading', { name: sharedCopy.errorSummary.title })
    ).toBeVisible()
claims.note: the test clears the arrival date at the port of entry, so the summary names the arrival-details card.

claims.statement: An amendment is started from the notification list and an amending notification's question pages can be opened directly by URL while the amendment is in progress.
claims.quote:
await amendFromList(page, reference)
    await page.goto(`${BASE}/notifications/${reference}/port-of-entry`)

claims.statement: There is no rulings or decisions ledger file in any of the four feature folders that end a notification.
claims.note: listed every file in the four folders; they hold only page.js, controller.js, template.njk, copy/, the fit spec, the co-located unit tests, declaration/test-support.js and confirmation/outstanding.js. The repo's design-decision records live in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/docs/page-design.md and src/server/app/docs/decisions.md, which other parts read.
